What Module 115 covers

One session for the whole plant: how it is started, run, stopped and protected. Five questions. Fri 06-Nov, 10:00–14:08.

  • Which route do I take, and who authorises it? Block 1
  • How do power and utilities come back first? Block 2
  • How does gas go from the inlet to dry, sweet gas? Blocks 3, 4
  • How do we go cold, make LNG and fill the tank, and restart a cold plant? Blocks 5, 7
  • How do compressors start and stop, what is normal, how do we stop, and what do the shutdown levels do when it goes wrong? Blocks 6, 8, 9

C-⁠AC1–C5

Utilities, flare pilots and hot oil on diesel power.

Pressurise V-⁠202 and V-⁠201 to 10 barg; FV-⁠2001 closed, no gas to Unit 330.

Unit 340: one ammonia compressor at a stable evaporating temperature.

C-⁠E released
F7

Move the fuel supply to treated gas through PV-⁠3732 for normal operation.

Start-up pressure.The initial start-up runs at reduced pressure: PIC-2001 at 10 barg through stages C-B to C-E and the first cool-down. When cool-down is reached in CB-356, raise PIC-2001 progressively to 40 barg (step D12).
Route
Verify before proceeding
Next procedure
Cold start
Complete readiness gates, utilities, Unit 200 pressurisation, fuel-gas transfer, treatment, refrigeration, dehydration and equipment preparation. Release each matrix stage.
C-A, C-B, F, C-C, C-D and C-E; then Section 21.6.
Warm start
Record retained utilities, inventories and the current cold-box condition. Recheck affected readiness gates, treatment quality and package checks; the supervisor records each omitted stage and the reason.
Applicable checks in C and F; Section 21.6.
Retained-cold restart
Confirm the cold-box temperature and pressure profile, inventory, utilities, protection and restart envelope against the restart plan.
Section 21.7; package-specific starts in Section 21.8.

Block 5 · Going cold · 1/7 — Part 21 §21.6 · route

The cool-down at a glance, and the commissioning boundary

GReadiness
BSIf power lost
C-AUtilities
C-BUnit 200
FFuel gas
C-CUnit 330
C-DUnit 340
C-EUnit 310

CD-BLoop

Commissioningbefore this procedure starts
Evacuation record: 70 Pa absolute
Vacuum decay test record: 12 h
Nitrogen vacuum break
CD-⁠AD1–D5

Confirm refrigeration and treated gas from Section 21.5; prepare MR inventory.

CD-⁠BD6–D9

Prove isolation, pressurise the loop and control the cooling ramp.

CD-⁠CD10–D14

Start gas circulation at the thermal trigger; establish first liquid and start the NRU.

TT1–T4

Accept the tank for receiving, then increase demand and hand over.

Critical sequence boundary. MR circuit evacuation, the vacuum decay test and the nitrogen vacuum break are commissioning and pre-commissioning activities. They are completed with the circuit isolated, under their own procedures, before this procedure starts. Run the compressor for refrigerant charging only after they are accepted and recorded and the package is ready for operation. A normal retained-inventory restart does not require MR evacuation.
Which route, what pressureUse this route for the first cryogenic operation, or when an assessment of the plant condition calls for a new cool-down. The cool-down runs at the 10 barg reduced-pressure condition until cool-down is reached in CB-⁠356 (D12).
Cold box and tankThe cold box and TA-⁠221 have separate cooling procedures. A ready cold box does not mean the LNG tank is ready. Tank drying, pressure and vacuum protection, and vendor-supervised initial cooling must be accepted before filling.
Trends to set upSet up continuous temperature trends for the cold-box stream inlets and outlets and the available metal and axial measurement points, so that the operator can see the largest temperature difference, the rate of change and any lost stream.

Normal operation — monitoring and response matrix

Entry conditions and operating checks. Confirm that the required flow, pressure, level and temperature loops are in automatic, compressor capacity control is enabled, and duty/standby selections are correct. Verify the live status of alarms, shutdown functions and bypasses against the authorised operating configuration.
Set pointA displayed set point alone does not confirm that its protective action is available.
System
Check / operating value
Confirmation / response
Sweetening
Monitor outlet CO2 on AT-⁠3301. Check absorber PT-⁠3311A/B/C and TT-⁠3301, TT-⁠3302, TT-⁠3307, TT-⁠3308 and TT-⁠3309.
Keep treated gas within the operating specification. Investigate breakthrough promptly using the unit response procedure; verify AAHH-⁠3301 availability.
Amine circulation
TDIC-⁠3301 / TV-⁠3301 controls lean-amine temperature; FIC-⁠3301 controls flow. Check E-⁠334 fan staging, levels in T-⁠331, T-⁠332, V-⁠334 and V-⁠332, and inventories in V-⁠335 and V-⁠336.
Confirm stable levels, active level control and sufficient make-up inventory. Confirm P-⁠332A/B duty/standby selection. Correct declining inventory before automatic make-up loses its supply.
Dehydration
Trend outlet moisture on AT-⁠3101: water ≤0.1 ppmv.
Investigate a rising moisture trend with the dryer cycle and regeneration temperature (TIC-⁠3122 235 °C).
Compressors: Units 340, 350, 360
Monitor oil differential pressure and header temperature; suction/discharge pressure and temperature on each running train.
Oil temperature 40–60 °C; oil differential trips below 1.5 bar. Investigate drift or loss of lubrication immediately using the package response procedure.
Compressor motor current
Monitor main motor current; each compressor unloads at its motor nominal current (PK-⁠341, PK-⁠351 HP/LP 535 A; PK-⁠361 327 A; PK-⁠362 155 A).
Confirm automatic unloading when demanded.
Mixed refrigerant
Check oil return valve operation: open at 60 °C; close at 40 °C while running.
Investigate a mismatch between temperature and valve state using the package procedure.
Cold box
Monitor stream-to-stream and stream-to-metal differences: less than 28 °C at any axial cross-section.
If one stream stops suddenly, stop the other streams immediately.
Power generation
Keep each gas engine above 30 % load; review running hours and available reserve.
Coordinate generator rotation and major load changes with electrical operations. Reconfirm the applicable load configuration before switching or starting another major consumer.
AT-3101 ≤0.1 ppmv. Same figure as the start-up quality criterion, which is not an alarm or trip setting.

Block 8 · Normal operation, shutdown, handover · 2/4 — Part 21 §21.11

Normal shutdown — coordination and end state

Objectives. A normal shutdown is a planned reduction of production followed by controlled equipment stops. Its objectives are to avoid abrupt electrical load changes, complete compressor post-lubrication, and leave each process section in a defined condition with the utilities it still needs.
End stateSelect and record the required end state before starting: a stopped cryogenic plant can remain cold and pressurised and is not automatically ready for a cold start or maintenance.
Order. Carry out the unit stops in the authorised shutdown order. Do not assume the order is simply the start-up sequence in reverse.
System
Before stopping
Completion check
Feed and treatment
Coordinate feed reduction with amine circulation, regeneration and dryer status.
Gas admission stopped; treatment equipment in the agreed retained or isolated condition.
LNG and BOG
Establish storage pressure control and a continuing vapour disposal route.
Tank pressure remains controlled throughout the shutdown.
Compressors
Coordinate process unloading with electrical load reduction; use the package stop sequence.
Main motors stopped and post-lubrication complete.
Heating and cooling
Keep circulation available during the required cooling period.
Dependent equipment has reached its approved stopping condition.
Utilities and protection
Retain power, air, nitrogen and emergency services for equipment that still needs them.
Final plant condition checked and handed over.
Plant Operating Procedures, Part 21 Rev. 02-R12 §21.11, §21.11.1, Table 21.13 Normal shutdown coordination, verbatim
Block 8 · Normal operation, shutdown, handover · 3/4 — Part 21 §21.11.3

Unit 330 shutdown — regeneration, cooling, isolation

Unit 330. Remove feed gas while retaining absorber pressure, then regenerate and cool the amine under the approved unit shutdown instruction.
DrainingBefore draining, confirm heating isolation, the required cooling endpoint, receiving capacity and the drain route. Do not drain a hot system or stop circulation while heat removal still requires it.
Step
Action / context
Release check / hold
1
Gradually close absorber inlet and outlet manual isolations to stop feed gas; retain absorber pressure.
Confirm feed flow stopped.
2
Continue amine circulation and regeneration with the remaining vessels under nitrogen; keep circulating for controlled cooling.
Confirm amine condition by sampling before draining.
3
Prepare heat removal, cooling and solvent recovery to V-⁠338-⁠1/-2 using the approved unit shutdown sequence.
Hold before draining. Verify heating isolated, cooling endpoint achieved, receiving capacity and drain line-up. Keep required circulation available until these conditions are met.
4
Stop reflux pumps P-⁠334A/B after the overhead system is depressurised and sufficiently cool; stop P-⁠332A/B after the lean amine loop is isolated.
Confirm the approved pressure and temperature endpoint, equipment condition and pump-stop order before proceeding.
5
Maintain the required positive nitrogen pressure in the regenerator; complete controlled depressurisation and amine recovery under the approved instruction. Vent residual absorber gas to flare.
Confirm flare availability, discharge route and the separate final pressure requirements for each vessel.
6
Close the relevant shutdown and block valves; verify the final unit condition and utility disposition.
Record the final pressure, temperature, inventory, isolation and nitrogen status. Resolve any deviation before handover.

Block 8 · Normal operation, shutdown, handover · 4/4 — Part 21 §21.12

The start-up / restart handover record

Acceptance. The supervisor accepts start-up when the route has reached its defined end state, the required quality and trends are stable, and receiving and electrical constraints are met. Record the following in the start-up log. Outgoing and incoming operators review it together and cross-check the plant indications.
Record
Required content
Route and progress
Route taken (black start, commissioning, first cool-down or retained-cold restart); approved plan revision; last completed step; date, time and responsible operators.
Protection and work
Current bypasses and authorisations; active alarms; outstanding permits and isolations; equipment unavailable; any deviation with owner and next action.
Power and utilities
Running generators; diesel generators stopped / available; fuel-gas route in use (PV-⁠3731 untreated or PV-⁠3732 treated); T1/T2/T3 states; island load and reserve assessment; voltage and frequency; air pressure and dew point; nitrogen and hot-oil conditions and burner fuel.
Treatment
Feed pressure, flow and pressure phase; amine inventory, temperature and flow; CO2 analyser result and validation; dryer bed and regeneration state; moisture result.
Cryogenic section
MR inventory and composition; running HP/LP and BOG packages; current cold-box temperatures, rates and differences; receiving and NRU status.
Storage and restart basis
TA-⁠221 pressure and level, usable receiving capacity and BOG destination; planned end state (stopped or running) and retained-condition evidence.
Acceptance
Supervisor acceptance; CRO and FO names and time; incoming operator cross-check.
HoldRecord the reason for any check not completed, and hold the dependent operation.
Plant Operating Procedures, Part 21 Rev. 02-R12 §21.12, Table 21.17 Start-up and restart handover record, verbatim

Block 9

When it goes wrong

Block 9 · When it goes wrong · 1/8 — C&E sheets · Manual §2.3

Four shutdown levels: ESD, PSD, LSD, ASD

ESDI1

Level I1, ESD: Emergency Shut Down in hazardous area

Causes

Six rows: push button, fire detection, spill detection, ESD from RTU.

Effects

Closes shutdown valves and liquid outlets. Trips compressors, pumps, heaters, GE-⁠001 to GE-⁠007. Starts GE-⁠008, GE-⁠009, P-⁠481 A/B. BDV opening is marked on this sheet only.

Common set of 88 marks

PSDI2

Level I2, PSD: Process Shut Down

Causes

Push button, detection, utilities, flare, refrigeration, gas quality, process trips.

Effects

The same on every row. Closes shutdown valves and liquid outlets. Trips compressors, pumps, heaters, GE-⁠001 to GE-⁠007. Starts GE-⁠008, GE-⁠009, P-⁠481 A/B. Opens FEV-⁠2001, FEV-⁠3110A, FEV-⁠3110C.

One set of 85 marks

LSDI3

Level I3, LSD: Local Shut Down

Causes

36 causes, in nine units: levels, pressures, temperatures on one item.

Effects

Each row closes valves or trips items on a short list.

1 to 6 marks a row

ASDI4

Level I4, ASD: LNG loading bay Abandon Shut Down

Causes

3 causes: ASD push button, loading bay gas, LNG spill detection at the impoundment.

Effects

Trips S-⁠221, S-⁠222. Opens DV-⁠7301, DV-⁠7303 on the impoundment row only.

Read each level on its own sheet. I1 to I4 are the labels in the sheet legend. The matrix does not say that one level includes another.
Who executes

“Siemens SIMATIC S7-⁠1500F fail-safe PLC”, “fully independent from the Plant Control System (PCS)”. Outputs per the Cause and Effect Matrix.

Actions (Manual, ESD system)

such as “isolation valve closure, depressurization, and equipment shutdown”

ESD to PCS

“The communication is strictly informational, and no safety logic depends on the PCS”

Letters on the rowsCCLOSEOOPENSSTART / ENERGIZEDTTRIP / DEENERGIZED
In the legend, on no rowAACTIVATE INTERLOCKISTART UP INHIBITPPERMISSIVERRESETVOVERRIDE

Block 9 · When it goes wrong · 7/8 — after any trip: next face

Common upsets and the first response

Upset
What the system does
First response
Where · who
Loss of instrument air
PALL-⁠5001 at 4 barg initiates PSD
Hold dependent start-up if air pressure is not stable. Restore instrument air, nitrogen and water for valve actuation, blanketing and process users.
C2, BS3FO / 500, 600, 530, 540
Unit 370 trip
A Unit 370 trip can cut supply to several consumers at once.
Check the Unit 370 shutdown and bypass status before relying on gas generation or gas-fired hot oil.
F note
Moisture off-spec, in operation
PSD item 15 MOISTURE HIGH LEVEL, AAHH-⁠3101.
Investigate a rising moisture trend with the dryer cycle and regeneration temperature (TIC-⁠3122 235 °C).
PSD, §21.10
CO2 off-spec, in operation
PSD item 16 CO2 HIGH LEVEL, AAHH-⁠3301.
Investigate breakthrough promptly using the unit response procedure; verify AAHH-⁠3301 availability.
PSD, §21.10
Compressor local shutdown
Its PK sheet row trips the compressor and the rest it marks.
Identify the initiating fault before resetting. Correct its cause and assess the effect on connected units.
PK sheets, §21.10.2
Upset
Response written in Part 21
Where · who
CO2 or moisture off-spec, start-up
Keep the outlet on the vent until CO2 is accepted. Keep off-spec gas out of the cold box.
C13, C18CRO / 330 · FO / CRO 330, 310
Power loss
After a loss of power, coordinate restoration with the electrical operator under the Unit 480 procedure. If power has been lost, restore the required supply under Section 21.4 before starting dependent equipment.
§21.4, §21.1
Cold-box stream stops
If a stream stops suddenly, stop the other streams immediately as the manufacturer recommends.
D9, §21.10CRO / 350
Unstable hot-oil flame
On unstable flame or poor condensate quality, return to gasoil under package control.
F6CRO / FO 410
Inlet pressure-control failure
Isolate feed and stabilise the downstream system. Use a bypass only if downstream pressure and flow control are effective.
C-⁠B note

Block 9 · When it goes wrong · 8/8 — Part 21 · cards G4, R1 · §21.10.2

After a trip: first-out, reset, choose the restart route

1Find the cause firstR1 · SS / CRO

Confirm why the plant stopped, which shutdown actions operated and whether maintenance or manual intervention changed the line-up.

BeforeShutdown log, first-out alarms and maintenance handbacks available; no active trip cause.

ProveShutdown cause cleared; affected systems and changed boundaries listed.

2Reset only afterG4, R1 · §21.10.2

G4Do not force a permissive or reset an unexplained trip.

R1A repeated or unexplained trip requires investigation before reset or restart.

PackageIdentify the initiating fault before resetting. If unresolved, keep the package stopped and investigate. Reset the local shutdown alarms in the PCS after correction. Verify the reset locally. If it fails, investigate the remaining cause before another attempt.

3Then choose the routebefore work begins, the supervisor (SS) records the plant condition and authorises the route.
Plant condition
Route
Completion
One compressor package stopped
Package start, Section 21.8. Recovery, Section 21.10.2
Trip cause cleared; auxiliaries ready; automatic start completed.
Cold box cold, inventories retained after a stop
Retained-cold restart, Section 21.7
Restart plan accepted for the measured temperatures, pressures and inventories.
Warm cold box or first cryogenic service
Controlled cool-down, Section 21.6
Equipment thermal limits respected; storage ready for LNG.
Section 21.7: after a controlled shutdown when the plant previously produced LNG, the cold box remains cold and the process inventories have been retained. A loss of containment, air ingress, uncertain moisture, lost MR inventory or an unrecorded thermal excursion means more preparation is required. The supervisor selects the re-entry point for each system; repeat preparation where equipment was opened, inventory was lost or the retained condition is unsuitable.
Package back is not plant back. A successful package restart does not mean the whole plant is ready. C&E Notes: “A complete unit shut down generate a Process Shut Down (PSD)”.
